data.name: Alo Murago Washed
data.story: Alo Murago is a washing station in the Guji zone of Ethiopia, where heirloom varieties are processed using traditional washed methods. The Guji zone is renowned for producing coffees with exceptional floral and fruit complexity at high altitudes.
data.reason: A washed heirloom from the Alo Murago station in Guji — representing the clean, floral baseline of one of Ethiopia's finest coffee zones.

data.name: Arjuna Natural Classic
data.story:
Gunung Arjuna rises in the highlands of East Java, where smallholder farmers cultivate Arabica on its volcanic slopes at 1,100–1,400 masl. The mountain's cool temperatures, fertile volcanic soils, and natural forest shade create conditions for a clean, sweet cup that's distinctly Javanese. Coffee cultivation on Arjuna has grown alongside reforestation efforts, with local communities planting coffee to restore the mountain's vegetation while creating sustainable livelihoods.

The farms around Arjuna are part of Java's expanding specialty Arabica movement, experimenting with honey, natural, and anaerobic processes to showcase the terroir of this underappreciated East Java origin.
data.reason: Arjuna's classic natural delivers tamarind, lemon zest, and cacao nibs — a traditional Javanese profile with earthy depth and citrus brightness. Chosen as a reliable, versatile Indonesian single origin.

data.name: Campo Hermoso Bourbon Sidra Honey
data.tagline: Floral, Candy, Blueberry, Tartaric Acidity, Azahar, Velvet Body, Juicy, Long Aftertaste, White Chocolate
data.story:
Finca Campo Hermoso is a 25-hectare farm in Circasia, Quindío, led by Edwin Noreña — a fourth-generation farmer, Q-grader, and head judge for the Colombian Cup of Excellence. With over 20 years in specialty coffee, Edwin is one of Colombia's pioneers in experimental processing and co-fermentation techniques inspired by the craft beer industry.

Edwin's innovation extends to adding dehydrated fruits and natural compounds to fermentation tanks, creating distinct flavor profiles that have earned international recognition. His Golden Washed Pink Bourbon contributed to a 2022 Micro-roaster of the Year win, and Campo Hermoso — alongside the renowned Santuario Project — has become a hub for fermentation research in Colombia.
data.reason: Edwin's Bourbon Sidra honey delivers floral, candy, blueberry, and white chocolate with a velvet body — a rare varietal cross processed with Edwin's signature technique. Selected for its extraordinary complexity and long aftertaste.
data.tastingNotes: Floral, Candy, Blueberry, Tartaric Acidity, Azahar, Velvet Body, Juicy, Long Aftertaste, White Chocolate

data.name: Colombia El Obraje Geisha Washed
data.story:
Hacienda El Obraje is located in the volcanic highlands of Nariño, Colombia, owned by Pablo Andrés Guerrero. Originally a 92-hectare wheat and grain farm, Pablo transitioned to specialty coffee and built his own processing facility by 2009. In 2011, he brought Geisha seeds from Panama, starting with 2,000 trees — today, over 9,000 Geisha trees thrive in Nariño's mineral-rich volcanic soils.

Pablo's dedication paid off spectacularly: he won the 2021 Colombia Cup of Excellence with a Washed Geisha scoring 90.61 points — the only finalist representing Nariño. The farm's high altitude at 2,200 masl and unique microclimate produce Geisha with exceptional clarity and complexity.
data.reason: El Obraje's washed Geisha is a study in purity — jasmine, citrus fruits, lime, peach, and grapefruit in a remarkably clean cup. We chose this coffee because Pablo Guerrero is one of the few producers growing world-class Geisha outside of Panama, and his 2021 Cup of Excellence win proved that Nariño's terroir can rival the best Geisha origins in the world.
data.tastingNotes: Jasmine, Citrus Fruits, Lime, Peach, Grapefruit

data.name: Colombia El Paraiso Geisha Natural
data.story:
Finca El Paraíso is the brainchild of Diego Samuel Bermudez, a visionary producer in Piendamó, Cauca, at 1,960 masl. What began as a small family farm has become a living laboratory for coffee processing innovation. Diego's journey shifted dramatically in 2015 when he placed first in a regional competition, and he went on to reach the Top 10 of the 2018 Colombia Cup of Excellence with a double anaerobic Bourbon and again counted among the 2019 winners with a washed anaerobic Castillo.

Together with his brother Alexander and cousin Cristian Zúñiga, Diego founded INDESTEC — a research company dedicated to optimizing coffee fermentation. Their pioneering use of thermal shock washing, controlled-temperature anaerobic tanks, and precise cherry selection has produced over 10 replicable, award-winning profiles. El Paraíso won two categories in the Colombia Land of Diversity competition and continues to set the standard for experimental processing in Colombian specialty coffee.
data.reason: This natural-processed Geisha from El Paraíso delivers the full fruit spectrum that Diego's controlled fermentation unlocks — grapefruit, yellow fruits, and lime with the signature floral blossoms. We chose it because natural El Paraíso lots are rare and highly sought after, and this one captures the farm's terroir in its most vivid, unfiltered form.

data.name: Costa Rica el Tirra Wush Wush Honey
data.story: El Tirra is sourced from the Tarrazu cooperative in Costa Rica's renowned Tarrazu region, at 1,600 masl. Tarrazu is widely considered one of the finest coffee-growing regions in Central America, where volcanic soils, high altitude, and cool Pacific winds create ideal conditions for specialty Arabica. The Wush Wush varietal — originally from Ethiopia's Kaffa region — is rare outside of Africa, making this an unusual and exciting offering.
data.reason: This Wush Wush honey from Tarrazu delivers eucalyptus, lemon, and honey — a rare Ethiopian varietal grown in Costa Rica's best terroir. We chose it because Wush Wush outside of Ethiopia is exceptionally uncommon, and the honey process adds a syrupy sweetness that complements the varietal's naturally herbal character.

data.name: El Diviso Chiroso Natural
data.story:
Finca El Diviso is a family farm in the mountains of Huila, Colombia, at 1,750–1,850 masl, run by Nestor Lasso alongside his brother Adrian and neighbor Jhoan Vergara. Nestor has been connected to coffee since childhood but was determined to pursue specialty coffee as a sustainable future — training at Colombia's leading coffee school, SENA, before taking over the family farm.

Rather than following traditional methods, Nestor invested in experimental fermentation protocols combining oxidation, anaerobic steps, and cherry lixiviates to build complexity. The farm's fertile volcanic soils and temperate Huila climate allow slow, even cherry development, making El Diviso an ideal site for rare varietals like Chiroso, Sidra, and Ombligon.
data.reason: Chiroso is one of Colombia's most exciting emerging varietals, and El Diviso's terroir brings out its best — delicate florals with grapes, watermelon, and berries. We chose this lot because Nestor's natural processing perfectly complements Chiroso's inherently floral and fruity character, creating a cup that's both elegant and expressive.

data.name: Ethiopia Arbegona Muntasha Washed
data.story:
Mullugeta Muntasha's story is one of specialty coffee's most remarkable. After years as a transport truck driver, he returned to his village in Arbegona, Sidama, in 2021 and began processing coffee at his Dawencho station, collaborating with 600 local smallholder farmers at altitudes reaching 2,000 masl and above.

Success came immediately and overwhelmingly: Mullugeta placed 2nd in the Cup of Excellence for the Dawencho farmer group and 6th under his own name. By 2022, four of the top 10 CoE winners were Mullugeta's lots — an extraordinary achievement for a producer who had only entered the industry a year earlier. His rapid rise speaks to both his natural talent and Arbegona's exceptional terroir.
data.reason: The washed Muntasha shows Arbegona's terroir in its purest form — jasmine, bergamot, peach, orange, and honey with delicate, tea-like clarity. We selected this lot because Mullugeta's washed processing reveals why Arbegona is emerging as one of Sidama's finest origins, and because four CoE top-10 placements in a single year is not something you see often.

data.name: Ethiopia Bensa Balachow Filter
data.story: Shaped by Bensa's high elevations and cool mountain climate, this lot reflects the patience of slow cherry maturation. The natural process extends that journey, allowing sweetness to deepen as the cherries dry intact. Floral aromatics lead the way before ripe mulberries and lively tangerine unfold, creating a profile that is both vibrant and gracefully composed.

data.name: Gayo Anaerobic Natural 300h
data.tagline: Berries, Concord Grapes, Red Apples, Dates
data.story:
Gayo coffee comes from the highlands of Bener Meriah in Aceh, northern Sumatra — one of Indonesia's most respected Arabica-producing regions. The Gayo Highlands' cool climate, mist-covered mornings, and volcanic soils slow cherry maturation, allowing sugars and organic acids to develop evenly within the beans.

Among Indonesia's most distinguished highland Arabicas, Gayo coffee is celebrated for its balance, clarity, and layered flavor structure — combining Indonesian depth with brighter acidity than most Sumatran origins.
data.reason: This 300-hour anaerobic natural pushes Gayo's fermentation to its limits — berries, concord grapes, red apples, and dates with a deep, lingering finish. We chose it for its intense, fruit-driven profile that showcases what extended anaerobic processing can unlock in Gayo's highland beans.
data.tastingNotes: Berries, Concord Grapes, Red Apples, Dates

data.name: Lunamova Natural Nitro Maceration 120H Espresso
data.story: When meticulous work at origin meets a shared vision, Indonesian coffee reveals its full potential, standing confidently alongside the world's favorites. Crafted exclusively for NiR Coffee, this private lot undergoes a 120-hour nitrogen-controlled resting stage before natural drying, unlocking a vibrant expression of its flavor profile, texture, and clarity. Roasted for espresso, it brews up smooth, complex, and beautifully balanced, leaving a lasting impression.
data.tastingNotes: Grape, Berries, Floral, Plum, Mandarin Orange
